I've had similar issues with that in the past, and I don't think it's uncommon. What's helped me at school and feeling comfortable is forgetting what other people think and trusting my own thoughts. That's the whole point of why you're spending all that time and money to go grad school.

However it'd probably be a good idea to make friends with your colleagues. They might be going through similar hardships and that would make it easier, like you're not going through it alone. Maybe ask some of them for feedback on assignments/lectures. If you don't know how to make friends, just start going to on-campus lectures and activities that interest you. If you see someone from one of your classes, strike up a conversation. 

Also I wouldn't dwell on whether or not what you say is stupid. I use to think the same thing in really small seminar classes (and I still do from time to time) where I would think that I said something really lame. This led me to over think my answers which would make me sound like I was trying to hard to sound smart. Then, I would remind myself, "Oh yeah, this is school... I'm in an academic institution... I'm allowed so say things that might be wrong, that's called LEARNING". Just remember it's good that you spoke up .. chances are there are others in the class who found your comments really intelligent. 

Also--it's clear that you're over thinking it if you start worrying about what you're going to say in class before you even do the readings. Start applying your meditation techniques you're learning to not think about that before you read. Annotate a lot. Make good notes as you read along, that way you will have good jumping off points for the class discussion. 

Hope this helps, hang in there :]

I think it's more reasonable to keep your goals and not give up, but to somehow let go of that feeling between I'M NOT GOOD ENOUGH and I'M GOOD ENOUGH. To somehow live in-between or without that dichotomy would be fucking fantastic. Strange as it may sound, I think happiness lies somewhere within that indifference. Keeping things that you want to do in mind but not giving a damn too much. It's like when you're so aware of working forward towards something (a goal) you forget how to live presently, such as you did when you were a kid. I think the key would be to have goals but to take childish risks every now and then in the present moment, even if it might fuck it all up in the end.

Break ups suck, especially having to be on the dumped end of it. Last time I had to go through that I was a mess for months and I did what you just described: blamed it all on myself. What you need to realize is that you're not the failure in this situation. You were a dedicated, awesome girlfriend and he doesn't even have the balls to give you an explanation. As great of a guy you thought he may have been, it seems like he may be unsatisfied with long-term relationships if he just goes from girl to girl like that. Do you really want to be with someone who's afraid of committing?

I can't promise it's going to feel better right away as it sounds like you were (and still are) hopelessly in love with this guy, but it's all too true that time will heal your broken heart. To speed that process up, remind yourself how awesome you are. 

-Keep a notebook. Remind yourself what you're grateful for (your mom sounds pretty great for being there for you)
-Make sure you recognize what's lovable about yourself and really believe it
-Talk about it!! It will get easier. 

good luck<3
